newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares tumble on market expansion fears.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares tumble on market expansion fears.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index tumbled 5.32 percent on Wednesday, on heavy selling triggered in part by rumours that China's securities authorities planned to accelerate the pace of A share listings next year, brokers said.
Profit-talking added to the retreat, they said.
Class B shares inched lower in sluggish trading due partly to market talk that Beijing was likely to lannch a crackdown on Chinese nationals buying B shares later this year, brokers said.
Class B shares are officially restricted to foreign investors, but in practice mainland Chinese investors have been playing the foreign currency stock market for a long time.

"Chinese investors will forego any big-scale trading until the China Securities Regulatory Commission makes a clear statement as to whether it will drive them out of the market," a broker at Guotai Securities said.
The B share index fell 0.40 point, or 0.46 percent, to close at 87.53 on turnover of HK$15.60 million, compared with HK$15.63 million on Tuesday.
The A share index dived 14.49 points to end at 258.05 on turnover of 5.41 billion yuan, compared with Tuesday's 5.93 billion yuan.
The composite index dipped 12.88 points, or 5.01 percent, to finish at 244.42.
On the B share market, recently-listed television tubes maker SEG was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.12, or 4.36 percent, to HK$2.63.
Motorcycle producer North Jianshe skidded HK$0.06, or 2.62 percent, to HK$2.23.
Shenzhen Properties slumped HK$0.06, or 2.51 percent, to HK$2.33.
Diesel engine maker Changchai continued its downward trend on profit-taking, brokers said. The issue edged down HK$0.13 to HK$5.07.
Shenzhen International Enterprise, which is involved in the retail and real estate sectors, slipped HK$0.06 to HK$2.44.
Shenzhen Petrochemical bucked the trend, rising HK$0.10, or 4.44 percent, to HK$2.35 on paper-thin volume of 100 million shares.
China Bicycle edged up HK$0.02 to HK$1.76 on the day's heaviest trade of 765,542 shares due to institutional support, one broker said.
Conglomerate Lionda was the worst A share performer, diving 0.81 yuan, or 10.14 percent, to 7.18 yuan.
Zhuhai Shining slid 0.60 yuan, or 9.23 percent, to 5.90 yuan.
Qinghai Department Store lost 0.65 yuan to 6.48 yuan. Zhonglian Construction Equipment fell 0.89 yuan to 8.90 yuan due to profit-taking, brokers said.
